correctness.rationale: The GP(8,3) host graph has 16 vertices and 24 edges. A set is an identifying code exactly when it hits all 16 closed neighborhoods and all 120 pairwise symmetric differences of closed neighborhoods. verify_cpp.cpp exhaustively tests all 65,536 masks against those constraints; verify_python.py independently checks actual vertex-signature sets. They produce precisely 584 codes of minimum size eight. One-token moves are exhaustively exactly the pairs of different weight-eight masks of XOR-weight two; requiring the changed vertices to be graph-neighbors distinguishes slides. Both enumerate all 864 slide edges and 2,496 jump edges with identical certificates; full BFS from each state verifies 97 slide components (488+96 isolates), giant-component radius 8 and diameter 10, and one connected jump component of radius 7 and diameter 8. Degree and frozen-state induced-edge distributions are also checked; exhaustive finite state exploration is an exact proof, not asymptotic extrapolation. The public package contains all sources and replayable certificates.

value.rationale: The distinguishing gap is not code-size enumeration: sensor-replacement reconfiguration of minimum identifying codes is motivated by literature but its fixed-host mobility may have many components. The Möbius–Kantor cubic symmetric 16-vertex graph supplies a natural benchmark with a striking and not a priori implied contrast: jumps connect all 584 optimum arrangements (radius 7, diameter 8), whereas adjacent moves trap 96 configurations and leave one 488-state component (radius 8, diameter 10). The split frozen classes by induced-edge count and degree-24 bipartition extremals give independently interpretable structure. Exact complete finite state and edge certificates make this a self-contained fact with uses as an exact benchmark for detecting immobility; no grander or unproven significance is claimed.
